scope: Every inventoried SHOULD/SHOULD NOT/RECOMMENDED paragraph has an explicit non-rejection policy. This does not mark its MUST clauses covered.

policies.policy: Specification terminology, not a document warning.
Names remain case-sensitive. Authors may apply a case-collision lint to resolved uniqueness scopes; the validator deliberately does not reject or warn on case-only distinctions.
Caller DocumentLoader owns retrieval and well-known schema identity; no implicit network access or dereferenceability warning.
DocumentLoader::inspect_reference receives the resolved Core.SchemaVersion. The caller chooses whether and how to use $schemaversion in retrieval.
Implemented namespace/qualifier/target-namespace filtering by the document resolver; no caller warning needed.
Document scope uniqueness is enforced. Global namespace uniqueness outside the supplied document graph is the author's responsibility and cannot be inferred by this crate.
Tolerant XML consumption preserves unknown collection nullability; strict 4.01 authoring requires the facet. Options-based JSON conversion rejects unrepresentable unknown nullability.
Absent facets/defaults stay absent. Callers must not infer an unprovided maximum length or service default.

Arbitrary precision decimal text is retained. Client precision limits, data editing and PATCH selection are caller responsibilities; the metadata validator does not reject a valid high-precision model.
Facet parsing accepts symbolic scale values case-insensitively and serialization emits lowercase values.
The service author selects IncludeInServiceDocument using runtime queryability; static validation cannot infer which query options a service requires.
Missing navigation bindings are accepted. Services may intentionally omit bindings; callers needing navigability warnings inspect resolved bindings against their routing requirements.

Tolerant profile parsing omits unavailable/invalid expression annotations; report APIs retain recovery diagnostics. Resolved annotation diagnostics do not invalidate tolerant semantic reports. Legacy parser APIs retain their original error behavior.

Unknown AppliesTo values are retained. Applicability diagnostics are available during annotation validation but do not invalidate tolerant reports; strict authoring keeps its stronger validation policy.

Metadata controls and default omission are output-size preferences. SerializationOptions selects metadata policy; explicit record types are retained when omission may change interpretation. Legacy output may retain computable fields.
